text:
raj: quick follow-up from the hedging RFC review — found a telemetry coupling issue that could make retries look like normal latency spikes. want to align on mitigation.
clare: tl;dr? what part of telemetry is the problem exactly? :thinking:
raj: when we hedge to a fallback model we emit two spans for a single logical request. our dashboards sum both which inflates p95 and doubles token counts in some alerts.
ben: saw this in prod test yesterday. example: request id `rq_abc123` showed ~1.8x token billing in the trace vs billing pipeline.
anna: can we tag the fallback spans with `hedge.logical_id` and have the billing join on that? or is that too heavy?
raj: tagging helps but we need a phased approach. immediate: mark fallback spans as `role=hedge` and exclude them from the default "token_total" aggregator. medium: add `logical_id` for precise joins. long: change UI to present hedged views.
mike: any perf risk to adding `logical_id`? that'll be a new header in the proxy and svc layers.
raj: small header (`X-Redwood-Logical-Id`) only on hedged child requests. routing layer already propagates trace id. overhead is negligible. bigger risk is indexing/selectivity in tracing backend.
ben: alternative: emit a single aggregated span at gateway level that represents the logical request lifetime, and keep child spans as debug-only. then dashboards use the aggregate by default.
clare: I like aggregate span for product metrics, but ops still want child-level visibility for root cause. can we keep both?
anna: proposal: default dashboards use `gateway.aggregate` metric; child spans carry `role=hedge` and `hedge.reason`. ops can toggle to see raw spans.
infra-bot: perf-test-run #42 completed: 2% increase in p99 under synthetic hedging load (1000 rps, 20% hedged). logs: `hedge.aggregate emitted` present.
ben: 2% p99 is acceptable. what's the plan for retry accounting? right now gateways retry count increments when child is issued, which doubles attempt metrics.
raj: switch retry_counter to be incremented only on the logical/aggregate object instead of per-child attempt. that keeps attempt distribution meaningful. child attempts still log `attempt=1,2` for debugging.
mike: edge-case: what if child attempts run across regions and billing happens in different clouds? the aggregate object needs a canonical region assignment to join costs.
anna: canonical region = origin gateway region. child attempts add `attempt_region`. billing join uses `logical_id + gateway_region` as key. works for cross-cloud.
clare: careful with long-lived hedging ( > 5s ) — we should emit intermediate aggregate heartbeats so tracing and billing don't think it's idle.
raj: agreed. emit `gateway.aggregate` start/heartbeat/finish events. heartbeat every 1s for streaming requests longer than 500ms.
ben: any changes needed to the streaming resume/retry protocol? current stream resume uses `resume-token` tied to specific child. with logical ids we need resume to be logically idempotent.
raj: good call. plan: resume tokens include `logical_id` and `child_id`. resume must validate logical ownership first, then accept child-specific offset. that allows a different child to resume if original child died.
mike: how do we avoid duplicate bytes when a second child resumes mid-token?
anna: gateway will track `logical_offset` per `logical_id`. resume must supply `resume_offset`. gateway checks `resume_offset >= logical_offset` and replays only missing bytes. if resume_offset < logical_offset gateway responds with `409 ResumeConflict` plus `logical_offset`.
clare: sounds reasonable. one more: instrumentation naming. avoid `retry_*` for hedging counters, use `attempt_*` and `hedge_*` to separate intentional hedges vs safety retries.
raj: noted. I'll update the RFC appendix with these counters and an example mapping.
ben: tiny nit — add a small example snippet for header propagation in the proxy:
```
X-Redwood-Logical-Id: rq_abc123
X-Redwood-Attempt: 2
X-Redwood-Hedge: true
```
clare: 👍 add a short note on rollout: flip a flag to start emitting `gateway.aggregate` and switch dashboards to use it, watch error budgets for 48h, then change billing join.
raj: plan: canary in us-east-1 for 24h, then eu-west-1, then global. ops and billing teams looped in. I'll open the follow-up PR with code pointers.
mike: thanks — also let's add a unit test for resume conflict behavior so we don't regress.
raj: added to checklist. will prod-deploy the canary after infra review.
infra-bot: deploy request opened: canary/hedge-telemetry-mitigation -> reviewer: @clare, @ben.
clare: I'll review later today.
anna: thanks all. :thumbsup:
